title: Noise operator splits along the last coordinate
statement:
Fix $\rho \in \bbr$ and a Boolean function $f \colon \{0,1\}^{n+1} \to \bbr$, and let $Af$ and $Df$ be the average and the half-difference of $f$ over its last coordinate, each a Boolean function on $\{0,1\}^n$. For every $x \in \{0,1\}^n$ and every bit $b$,
\[
  T_\rho f(x, b) \;=\; T_\rho(Af)(x) \;+\; \sigma(b)\,\rho\,T_\rho(Df)(x),
\]
where $(x,b) \in \{0,1\}^{n+1}$ is the point obtained by appending $b$ as the last coordinate, $\sigma$ is the sign encoding, and $T_\rho$ is the noise operator.
hypotheses_covered: f is a Boolean function on n+1 variables
x is a point of the n-dimensional cube
replaced:
For $f : \{0,1\}^{n+1} \to \bbr$ the noise operator splits over the last coordinate:
\[
  T_\rho f(\mathrm{snoc}\,x\,b)
  = T_\rho(\mathrm{avgLast}\,f)(x) + (-1)^b\,\rho\,T_\rho(\mathrm{diffLast}\,f)(x),
\]
where $\mathrm{avgLast}\,f$ and $\mathrm{diffLast}\,f$ are the average and difference of
$f$ over the last bit.
